company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year over year. Management struck a cautiously optimistic tone, noting improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and saying they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 sales growth.

Cognex announced it will acquire RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the robotics and AI-driven machine vision space.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even without tariff refunds — ex-refunds EPS was 42 cents, still above consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year over year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS range of $1.85–2.15 was left unchanged and FQ2 EPS guidance is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings extensive CFO experience from Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The leadership change is largely a routine transition event with no financial guidance implications announced.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year over year to 12.4% vs. the Street's 13.85% — more than offsetting slightly better-than-expected revenues of $2.311 billion. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation pressuring household budgets, and expects a relatively flat retail sales environment in fiscal 2027 with no formal guidance until later this fall. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, ongoing structural cost actions, and a ~75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The result is a significant clinical milestone that reinforces VK2735 as a competitive candidate in the high-stakes GLP-1 obesity market. This trial readout is a major positive catalyst for the stock.

sectors: RV/recreational vehicle sector faces headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation are pressuring consumer demand and retail sales, with formal fiscal 2027 guidance deferred to later in the fall. The machine vision and robotics space gets a lift from Cognex's acquisition of RealSense, signaling consolidation around Physical AI and depth-sensing technology.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday, September 22nd, with several names reporting before the open. No broad macro or Fed commentary in today's note — let's go straight through the movers.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat on earnings per share — fifty-six oh five versus the Street at fifty-four oh three — but the quality of that beat is the story here. The upside was almost entirely driven by tariff refunds, which added 145 basis points to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture gets messier. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus the Street expecting plus 3.1% — a meaningful miss — and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year over year. Management did note improving sales linearity late in the quarter and says they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027. This is a mixed print — the headline beat, but the internals are soft.

Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly five hundred million upfront plus another hundred and six and a half million. RealSense is expected to do eighty to ninety million in revenue, growing more than 50% year over year. This is a clear strategic move deeper into robotics and AI-driven vision — bullish for Cognex.

MillerKnoll delivered a genuine earnings beat — 53 cents versus 36 cents expected — and importantly, they would have beaten even without tariff refunds. Ex-refunds, EPS was 42 cents, still well above consensus. Sales missed at 923 million versus 943 million expected, but orders were up 3.5% year over year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed modestly, but EPS guidance held and the second quarter midpoint is in line with the Street. Call it a mixed-to-positive print.

THOR Industries missed. EPS came in at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year over year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85%. Management's tone was cautious — citing stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets through the key selling season. They expect flat retail in fiscal 2027 and won't give formal guidance until later this fall. On the positive side, dealer inventory is lean, structural cost actions are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year over year. Net-net, this is a bearish print with a few green shoots.

Pentair named a new CFO — Bob Hau, effective November 1st. He comes from Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Routine leadership transition, no financial implications announced.

And the headline mover this morning is Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking pre-market after positive trial results for their GLP-1 drug VK2735 showed 22% weight loss. That is a strong clinical readout and puts Viking firmly on the map as a real competitor in the obesity drug space. Clearly bullish.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the momentum story. AutoZone is a low-quality beat — watch how the market prices the comp miss. THOR confirms the consumer discretionary pressure in big-ticket rate-sensitive categories. And Cognex is making a bold AI-adjacent bet. No macro catalyst flagged for today's session in this note — trade the individual stories.
